goal: Bind compiled gate execution to the audited plugin witness installation
asset: Compiler provenance, attest rows and launch/record preflight
scope: Pinned witness commands and detached child verification
Producer identity in every new attest row
Launch and resume refusal on missing or changed pin
Citation mismatch on another witness producer
outOfScope: Authenticating against deliberate source or log forgery
Automatic plugin installation or update rollback

record.question: How should a graph keep its execution witness stable across plugin updates?

options.strongest_objection: Moving or editing the installation requires explicit recompile and re-audit
A running graph silently changes its witness semantics on auto-update

record.rationale: Pin entry points and aggregate execution helpers by content, carry the producer into rows and compare it with the compiled expectation.
evidence: Issue #183 measured a 1.43 graph whose gate ran under 1.45 after an update
Current preamble names no root and rows omit producing code identity

costs.cost: Hash the small script directory at compilation and witness startup; preserve a pinned installation for in-flight runs
evidence: Script bytes are local files and existing compiler metadata and witness rows carry JSON

costs.cost: Unreviewed witness drift during an in-flight campaign
evidence: Issue #183 recorded attest row att_ee42302855d3 from a different installation

requirements.statement: Compiled prove/cited gates use one content-pinned installation; changed or missing files refuse launch and execution; every new row names its loaded producer and mismatched citations refuse a clean record
requirements.counterexample: A cached graph compiled under one installation runs or records a gate from an updated installation as ATTESTED

checks.scope: Real source files, emitted graph metadata, witness CLI, producer persistence and citation checks
assumptions: The filesystem and Python interpreter are trusted; a malicious actor able to rewrite pins and logs is outside this provenance boundary

challenges.claim: Are hashes of entry points alone sufficient when helpers change?
challenges.resolution: The pin also includes an aggregate hash of every Python and shell helper in the installation scripts directory.
